source_name: Drustvo Mali delnicarji Slovenije (skupaj.si / malidelnicarji.com) — bank AGM materials and shareholder filings
why_relevant: Minority-shareholder association that archives skupscina (AGM) convocations, management reports and shareholder disputes for unlisted Slovenian banks (Gorenjska banka, Delavska hranilnica, Primorska hranilnica, LON, Addiko, Intesa, SKB). For banks with no IR function, AGM materials are often the only place strategy and network plans surface.

source_name: Slovenian business press coverage of bank results (Vecer, Forbes Slovenija/N1, Zurnal24)
why_relevant: Results coverage frequently quotes figures banks state in briefings but do not publish in a machine-readable form (e.g. 'largest branch/ATM network in Slovenia', ~450 shared ATMs, profit and revenue splits). Useful as an early signal and as a pointer to the underlying press release, but must always be traced back to the primary report.

source_name: financialreports.eu — aggregated filings for NLB and Addiko Bank AG
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator that indexes ESEF/regulated filings for European listed issuers including both listed banks in this cell. Convenient normalised discovery layer when issuer sites reorganise their PDF paths; not a substitute for primary filings.

source_name: ZBS — Članice (member directory: banks, savings banks, leasing companies)
why_relevant: Authoritative actor map: lists member banks/savings banks (NLB, SKB, OTP, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, Addiko, Sparkasse, BKS, Delavska hranilnica, Direktna banka, SID, GB, Ljubljanska banka, Probanka) and a separate leasing-company tier (BKS Leasing, DH Leasing, Mobilize Financial Services, Toyota/Volvo/Scania Finance, SKB Leasing, Sparkasse Leasing, NLB Lease&Go). The leasing tier reveals consumer-finance actors that a pure bank register does not label.

source_name: ZBS — Podatki bančnega sektorja (banking sector indicators)
why_relevant: Association-curated sector indicators (number of banks, employees, balance-sheet total, ROA/ROE, corporate and household loans/deposits). Sourced from Banka Slovenije but pre-aggregated into a stable time-series presentation — a convenient market-structure baseline. Note: observed as chart images, not machine-readable payment/card/ATM data.

source_name: ZBS — Sporočila za javnost in novice (press releases / position statements)
why_relevant: Where the sector's collective lobbying position is stated: observed items on cash accessibility ('Bančni sektor podpira dostopnost gotovine, želi pa, da bo rešitev dolgoročno vzdržna in pravična'), digital euro pilot participation, instant payments, contactless limits and card-fraud alerts. Directly quantifies/locates sector pain points on cash access and ATM network economics.

source_name: ZBS — Letna poročila (annual reports, 2001–2025, SL+EN)
why_relevant: 25-year run of association annual reports describing working committees (incl. payments), sector developments and priorities. Best longitudinal narrative record of how the SI banking industry framed payments/cash issues year by year; EN versions exist from ~2014.

source_name: Bančni vestnik — e-arhiv (banking journal archive, 1952–2026, ISSN 0005-4631)
why_relevant: The association's peer-style banking journal, with a searchable archive back to 1952 filterable by year, issue, category and author, plus a 'Brezplačni članki' free tier and English special issues. Practitioner articles on payment systems, cards, instant payments and cash are the deepest SI-language analytic layer outside the central bank.

source_name: ZBS — Plačilni promet / programska orodja (payment standards & tools)
why_relevant: The association is the de facto national standards-setter for interbank payment plumbing: UPN QR specification and registered-issuer tooling, ISO 20022 XML + TKDIS conversion tool, IzvrsbeXML standard for garnishment data exchange, SEPA creditor-identifier generator, and the payment-purpose code register (šifrant kod namenov plačil). Reveals the technical rails and which vendors/issuers integrate with them.

source_name: ZBS — SEPA section
why_relevant: Association-maintained SEPA hub; ZBS member banks and savings banks are the adherents to EPC SCT/SDD schemes, so this page is the local mapping of which SI institutions participate in which scheme — useful for scheme-adherence coverage that EPC lists render only at pan-EU level.

source_name: ZBS — Smernice / Kodeks / Standardi in priročniki (guidelines, code, standards)
why_relevant: Self-regulatory layer: sector code of conduct plus guidelines and manuals that banks apply collectively. Self-regulation often precedes or substitutes for regulation on fees, cash access and consumer disclosure, so these documents mark where the industry chose to bind itself.

source_name: ZBS — ABC bančnih izrazov (banking terminology glossary) + FAQ for bank customers
why_relevant: Authoritative SL↔EN banking/payments glossary maintained by the association — the cleanest way to build the local-language query vocabulary (kartično poslovanje, plačilna kartica, bankomat, POS terminal, provizija, takojšnja plačila) used across every other source in this run.

source_name: Trgovinska zbornica Slovenije (TZS) — Chamber of Commerce (retail/trade)
why_relevant: The merchant-side association (founded 17 Nov 2006), representing retailers — the acceptance side of card economics. It sits on the National Payments Council and maintains a 'Nacionalni svet za plačila' briefing page for members, plus a T-Informacije bulletin. This is where merchant-service-charge / interchange grievances and POS acceptance costs are articulated on behalf of SI retail.

source_name: Gospodarska zbornica Slovenije (GZS) — Podjetniško-trgovska zbornica (PTZ)
why_relevant: GZS is an NSP member; its PTZ branch chamber represents small business and trade — the SME merchant constituency most exposed to POS acceptance costs and cash handling. Publishes interest-representation ('Zastopanje interesov') material, collective agreements and governance/board composition that maps the retail actor set.

source_name: GZS — Združenja / zbornice dejavnosti (branch association directory)
why_relevant: Master index of ~30 GZS branch chambers, each a potential sector-specific source. For payments the relevant nodes are PTZ (trade), ZIT (informatics & telecoms — where payment-tech vendors and integrators sit), Zbornica poslovno storitvenih dejavnosti, Zbornica računovodskih servisov (fiscalisation/POS-software angle) and Združenje zavarovalnih posrednikov. Snowball entry point.

source_name: GZS — Združenje za informatiko in telekomunikacije (ZIT)
why_relevant: ICT branch association whose members include the systems integrators and software houses that build/deploy POS, fiscalisation and payment-acceptance software in Slovenia. Member lists and events reveal the vendor layer around ATM/POS estates that no bank register exposes; the ZITex export section flags SI payment-tech firms selling abroad.

source_name: Obrtno-podjetniška zbornica Slovenije (OZS) — Chamber of Craft and Small Business
why_relevant: Represents micro-merchants and craftspeople — the segment where cash-vs-card economics bite hardest and where mobile/softPOS adoption is being pushed. Observed positions supporting digital payments and mPOS for small traders, plus guidance on cash-handling rules (e.g. the €5,000 cash-acceptance ceiling). Regional OOZ chapters republish operational guidance, giving a second harvestable layer.

source_name: Zveza potrošnikov Slovenije (ZPS) — Slovene Consumers' Association
why_relevant: Independent non-profit consumer body and NSP member. Operates a free bank-fee comparison tool covering 15 banks and savings banks, refreshed roughly every two months, plus market reviews on basic payment accounts, card choice and ATM withdrawal costs (incl. DCC losses). This is the only regularly-updated cross-bank retail pricing aggregation outside the central bank's annual comparison.

source_name: Odbor za shemo Flik (Flik scheme committee) / Flik scheme, operated with Bankart
why_relevant: A bank-collective scheme body: competing SI banks formed the Flik instant-payment scheme with an inter-bank committee setting common rules, technically run by Bankart on the Bips IP infrastructure. The 'Odbor za shemo Flik' sits on the National Payments Council in its own right. Publishes adoption figures (~776k active users, ~80k added in 2025) and merchant onboarding rules — collective payment data no single bank publishes.

source_name: Združenje Povezani smo — cash-rights advocacy association
why_relevant: Civil-society association that collected 56,000+ signatures (2023) for a constitutional right to use cash, culminating in a National Assembly constitutional amendment (reported 67–1) enshrining the right to use cash in banking and legal transactions. Materially changes the SI cash-access policy environment — a hard constraint on branch/ATM rationalisation and on any cashless-acceptance strategy. Caveat: an activist body with unrelated campaigns; treat as an actor, not as a data source, and corroborate.

source_name: ZBS — Izobraževalni programi (training portal)
why_relevant: The association's training catalogue is a low-noise demand signal: which payments/cards/AML/fraud topics banks are collectively paying to be trained on, and which named practitioners lecture on them (a route to expert identification and to emerging operational pain points before they surface in position papers).

source_name: GZS media channels — Glas gospodarstva / media.gzs.si
why_relevant: GZS's own magazine and media portal carry business-side commentary and event reports (e.g. accessibility-of-services consultations) that surface chamber positions in fuller narrative form than press releases, including on payment accessibility and digitalisation of retail.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — corporate site (Podjetje / company profile)
why_relevant: Bankart is the domestic card switch/processor owned by Slovenian banks; its own pages state operating scale (card volumes, POS/ATM networks managed, SEPA volumes) and corporate/ownership structure. This is the ecosystem core with no banking-report equivalent.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — annual reports (Letno poročilo) PDFs
why_relevant: Audited annual reports of the domestic processor contain revenue, transaction/processing volumes, number of cards and terminals processed, ownership shares of member banks, and business commentary on the SI card market. The 2019 report explicitly compares Bankart-processed POS count against Bank of Slovenia totals — a rare direct market-share datapoint.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Poravnava kartic (card settlement system page)
why_relevant: Central bank description of the domestic card clearing/settlement system operated by Bankart (Mastercard, Karanto, BA/Maestro at POS and ATMs) and its settlement in TARGET2-Slovenija. Authoritative on which schemes/rails clear domestically and who operates them.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Upravljavci plačilnih sistemov (register of payment system operators)
why_relevant: Authoritative register naming every licensed payment-system operator in SI (Bankart, Activa/Intesa-operated system, etc.). Best pointer for keeping the actor map of switches/schemes current, and for detecting entries/exits.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Statistična poročila / Finančne institucije in trgi
why_relevant: Publishes the semi-annual SI payment/card statistics releases (cards issued by type, ATM count and contactless share, POS terminal count and growth) — the national denominator against which scheme/processor claims are benchmarked.
